parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires power-on to HumanDriving, HumanDriving → Autonomous on front_distance > 10, Autonomous to have sub-states AutoInitial/AutoFinal, return to HumanDriving on human steering command, brake pressed, or when in AutoFinal, and power-off to final from any state. The PlantUML model implements power-on, the front_distance transition, and the sub-machine structure, but handles power-off and the return-to-human-driving conditions incorrectly and adds an unspecified entry label.

issues.issue: Power-off transition is only defined from HumanDriving
issues.reason: Spec 5 says 'when power off, it will transit to final state'. The model only allows Power Off from HumanDriving. If the system is in Autonomous or one of its sub-states AutoInitial/AutoFinal, power off has no defined transition to the final state [*].

issues.issue: Return to HumanDriving is modelled as a single composite-level transition with a guard 'in (AutoFinal)'
issues.reason: Spec 4 says transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final). The model uses one exit transition from the composite Autonomous with an OR guard that includes 'in (AutoFinal)'. In UML a state-dependent return should be modelled as a transition originating from the AutoFinal sub-state, not as a guard on the composite exit. This mis-represents when the automatic return on reaching AutoFinal occurs and conflates the three triggers on the composite level.

issues.issue: Unspecified entry transition into the Autonomous sub-machine
issues.reason: Spec 2 requires autonomous mode to have sub-states and be a sub machine state, but does not specify an explicit 'Enter Autonomous Mode' trigger for [*] --> AutoInitial. The model adds a labelled entry transition that is not required by the specification and obscures the implicit entry to the first sub-state on entry to Autonomous.
issues.where: state Autonomous { [*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode ... }

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
